samples.name: Atsá
samples.why: Crater floor lava rock: dates the floor and records its interaction with water.

samples.name: Skyland
samples.why: Delta front sandstone. Its twin now sits in the Three Forks sample depot.

samples.name: Hazeltop
samples.why: Fine-grained mudstone from an ancient lake: best kind of rock to preserve organics.

samples.name: Bearwallow
samples.why: Paired lake-mudstone core from the delta front.

samples.name: Mageik
samples.why: Sulfate-bearing delta rock: evidence of evaporating water.

samples.name: Atmo Mountain
samples.why: Loose surface material: key for dust hazards to astronauts and equipment.

samples.name: Otis Peak
samples.why: Phosphate-bearing rock from the upper delta fan.

samples.name: Pilot Mountain
samples.why: Coarse river deposit carrying pebbles from outside Jezero.

samples.name: Pelican Point
samples.why: Upper fan boulder deposit from a high-energy flood.

samples.name: Comet Geyser
samples.why: Carbonate from the crater margin: records past climate and water chemistry.

samples.name: Sapphire Canyon
samples.why: Neretva Vallis riverbed rock with "leopard spots": potential biosignature (Nature, 2025).

samples.name: Silver Mountain
samples.why: First crater-rim sample: likely the oldest rock collected.
